name: DDD & Clean Architecture
when_applicable: Projects with domain logic separated from infrastructure, or projects that should have such separation

criteria.criterion: No inner layer imports from an outer layer (domain does not import infrastructure, application does not import frameworks)
criteria.how_to_test: Grep imports in domain/ and application/ directories — none should reference infrastructure/, frameworks/, or delivery-mechanism code

criteria.criterion: Entity and value object classes have zero framework imports (no ORM decorators, no HTTP types, no serialization annotations)
criteria.how_to_test: Read entity/model files in domain layer — check for imports from SQLAlchemy, Django ORM, FastAPI, Express, Prisma, etc.

criteria.criterion: Repository interfaces (abstract classes or protocols) are defined in the domain/application layer, not in infrastructure
criteria.how_to_test: Find repository interface definitions — they should live in domain/ or application/, with implementations in infrastructure/

criteria.criterion: Each use case / interactor does exactly one thing (no god-services with 10+ methods)
criteria.how_to_test: Count public methods per use-case/service class — should be 1-2 per class. Flag any with 5+.

criteria.criterion: Use cases receive/return plain DTOs or domain objects, not HTTP requests, ORM models, or framework types
criteria.how_to_test: Check use case method signatures — input/output types should be domain objects or simple DTOs, not Request/Response objects

criteria.criterion: Code uses domain expert terminology — class names, method names, and variables reflect the business language, not technical jargon
criteria.how_to_test: Compare naming in domain layer against business concepts. Flag generic names (Manager, Handler, Processor, Data, Info) in domain code.

criteria.criterion: Different bounded contexts have separate models — no single model shared across unrelated domains
criteria.how_to_test: Check if the same entity class is imported across multiple unrelated modules/services. Each context should define its own representation.

criteria.criterion: External system integrations go through an anti-corruption layer — external models are translated to domain models at the boundary
criteria.how_to_test: Find external API clients or SDK usages — they should return domain objects, not raw external DTOs leaked into domain logic

criteria.criterion: Child entities within an aggregate are only accessed through the aggregate root, not directly from repositories
criteria.how_to_test: Check repositories — they should only load/save aggregate roots. No repositories for child entities within an aggregate.

criteria.criterion: Value objects are immutable — no setters, no mutation methods. Equality is by attributes, not identity.
criteria.how_to_test: Find value object classes — check for frozen dataclass, __eq__ by value, no mutable state. Flag setters or mutation methods.

criteria.criterion: Side effects are triggered via domain events, not inline method calls from the aggregate
criteria.how_to_test: Check if significant state changes emit events (OrderPlaced, PaymentReceived) rather than directly calling notification/email/external services.

criteria.criterion: Domain entities contain behavior (methods with logic), not just data fields with getters/setters
criteria.how_to_test: Check entity classes — they should have methods that enforce business rules, not just property access. Flag entities that are pure data bags with all logic in services.

criteria.criterion: Ports (driven and driving) are defined as interfaces/protocols/abstract classes, not concrete implementations
criteria.how_to_test: Find port definitions — they should be abstract (Protocol, ABC, interface). Concrete code depends on the abstraction, not the implementation.

criteria.criterion: Adapter implementations live outside the application core (in infrastructure/ or adapters/ directories)
criteria.how_to_test: Check that concrete implementations of ports (PostgresRepo, StripeGateway, etc.) are not co-located with domain/application code

criteria.criterion: Concrete adapters are injected at composition root (startup/main), not instantiated inside use cases
criteria.how_to_test: Check use case constructors — they should receive interfaces, not instantiate concrete implementations. Look for 'new PostgresRepo()' inside business logic.

criteria.criterion: Controllers/handlers contain only input parsing, use-case invocation, and response formatting — no business logic
criteria.how_to_test: Read controller/route handler code — flag if-else chains, calculations, or domain rule enforcement happening at the delivery layer

criteria.criterion: Data crossing layer boundaries uses explicit DTOs or mappers — domain objects are not directly serialized to HTTP/DB
criteria.how_to_test: Check API responses and DB queries — domain entities should be mapped to response DTOs, not returned directly. ORM models should be mapped to domain objects.

criteria.criterion: Domain and application logic can be unit-tested without booting any infrastructure (DB, HTTP, queues)
criteria.how_to_test: Check test files for domain/application layer — they should use in-memory fakes or mocks, not require real DB connections or HTTP servers
